description: GATE AUDIT: /readyz answers HTTP 200 even while its body reports the dependency down — the grader's own first check passes on the broken endpoint, which is why a gate has to be read rather than trusted by its name
command: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:8080/readyz 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^200$' && echo pass || echo fail

description: GATE AUDIT: the code-path check is the one that actually measures the repair — it counts 1 on the fixed readiness code and 0 on the unfixed, unlike the HTTP-status check which cannot tell them apart
GATE AUDIT: the second discriminating surface — the Helm readiness probe path — is /healthz, so the repair holds where the cluster actually calls it and not only where the code does
command: python3 -c "import re,sys;t=open('platform/helm/orders-api/values.yaml').read();m=re.search(r'readinessProbe:.*?path:\s*(\S+)',t,re.S);sys.exit(0 if m and m.group(1)=='/healthz' else 1)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail
